name: Gusset fin
summary: A triangular reinforcing rib in the corner between a vertical wall and the face it stands on, built in layers stacked perpendicular to its hypotenuse.

evidence.label: EXPERIMENTAL
evidence.scope: Deterministic generator validated by schema, geometry-bounds, and golden-output tests, including that the final layer reproduces the hypotenuse exactly. Not yet evidenced on physical hardware. Note that the coordinated-xyz-motion capability this requires is itself only EXPERIMENTAL on the reference Dobot machine, whose manifest records a KNOWN limitation around layer-boundary transitions on long continuous runs — that concern applies directly to this operation and is not resolved by it.

length.description: The leg running out along the base face, from the corner outward (+X in the operation's own frame).

height.description: The leg running up the wall from the corner (+Z in the operation's own frame).

thickness.description: Fin thickness, across Y and centered on it. Rounded to a whole number of beads at settings.beadWidth; one bead is the default and the usual case for a gusset.

baseZ.description: Z the base face already reaches — the height of whatever this fin stands on. This operation does not generate that support; see `dependencies`.

inputs.description: A right triangle with legs `length` and `height` meeting at the corner, which is the operation's own origin. Layers stack along the perpendicular from that corner to the hypotenuse, so the first layer is a short segment in the corner and the last is the hypotenuse itself, laid in one pass.

dependencyNotes: Not a hard runtime dependency of the generator, which only needs baseZ. Documents the intended composition: a plan builds the base face and the wall the fin braces (typically with layer-filling) and then places one invocation of this operation per fin, using the process plan's `at` field to rotate each around the wall. The fin's inner edge is a straight chord, so against a *curved* wall such as a pipe boss the plan should seat it on the best-fit chord rather than the nominal radius — see README.md.

validation.description: Every emitted point stays inside the declared triangle: x in [0, length], z in [baseZ, baseZ + height], y within half the thickness.
The last layer's pass runs corner to corner, from (0, baseZ + height) to (length, baseZ) — the hypotenuse in a single straight stroke.
Each layer's pass is longer than the one before it, so the triangle genuinely stands on its tip.
Every Fin layer stroke changes Z along its own length. Fin connection paths join adjacent strokes along the base or wall face.
Emits a `warnings` entry when height exceeds length, tipping the build direction past the ~45 degree unsupported-overhang guideline used across FDM printing generally.
